cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has a new burden, and this one is against the Valley of Vision. The whole town has gone up to the rooftops, and he wants to know what ails them now. Friend, when EVERYBODY in town is on the roof at the same time, that's not a view. That's a situation.
Isaiah calls it a city of commotion, a town of revelry. And this town has its dead, but here's the strange part.

cards.question: True or false: the dead of the Valley of Vision were killed in battle.
Nobody in the Valley of Vision died in battle. True or false: the town's rulers stay and fight it out.
The rulers run off together, and others flee to a distant place. How does it go for all of them?

cards.text: The destruction of the daughter of his people breaks the prophet. He says he needs to weep bitterly.

cards.question: Weeping over the destruction of his people, the prophet tells others not to try to console him.

cards.text: Here's why he weeps. A day has been set for the Valley of Vision: tumult, trampling and confusion, walls broken down and crying to the mountains.

cards.question: A day of tumult and trampling and confusion is set for the Valley of Vision. Who set it?

cards.text: Then foreign lands gear up. Elam takes up a quiver, with chariots and horsemen, and Kir uncovers the shield, which is the battle version of cracking your knuckles real slow.

cards.question: With Elam and Kir ready for war, the choicest valleys around the city fill up with ___, and horsemen are posted at the gates.

cards.text: Now the burden names names: Judah. Its defenses are uncovered, and on that day, the people go looking for something to lean on.

cards.question: Judah's defenses are uncovered. On that day, where do the people look?

answers.text: The weapons in the House of the Forest
The prophets serving in the temple

cards.text: They see many breaches in the walls of the City of David. They collect water from the lower pool too. That's the whole house running around five minutes before the guests show up.

cards.question: To strengthen the wall, the people count the houses of Jerusalem and tear them down.
Jerusalem even builds a reservoir between the walls for the waters of the ancient pool. What does Isaiah say the people did not do?

answers.text: Look to the One who made it

cards.question: With the city in danger, on that day the Lord GOD of Hosts called for ___ and wailing, for shaven heads and the wearing of sackcloth.
The people of Jerusalem answer the Lord's call by putting on sackcloth and mourning.

cards.text: Instead there's joy and gladness, butchering of cattle, slaughtering of sheep, eating of meat and drinking of wine, and the motto of the day is "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!" God sent out a call to weep, and they turned it into a block party.

cards.question: Then the LORD of Hosts speaks in the prophet's hearing: until your dying day, this sin of yours will ___ be atoned for.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the breaches in the walls, the water from the lower pool, and the joke about guests showing up. Only the opening card may run to three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "The king of Assyria" and "The king of Babylon" can be argued as right. Historically, a foreign king's army brought the tumult on Jerusalem, and Elam and Kir (22:6) are named as the attackers. A baker who knows that history could argue for either answer. The wrong answers should be ones no baker could defend as the one who set the day.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 2 says the town has its dead "but here's the strange part," right before card 3 asks whether the dead were killed in battle. Flagging the expected answer as strange tells the baker it's False, so the setup rules out the wrong answer instead of giving context to reason from.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 10 says Elam comes "with chariots and horsemen." Card 11 then asks the baker to fill in "___, and horsemen are posted at the gates." Since card 10 already paired chariots with horsemen, it gives away the answer to card 11.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
